mechanics.function: Orient the audience within an ongoing series
mechanics.mechanic: Briefly summarize the preceding installments, then explain why the current topic extends or completes that sequence.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when an episode, chapter, or lesson belongs to a larger curriculum and returning readers need context.
mechanics.avoid: Do not spend so long recapping earlier material that the new subject feels delayed.

mechanics.mechanic: Address likely objections or assumptions from different audience segments, then show how the topic applies to each group.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when the subject appears specialized, unappealing, or relevant only to experts.
mechanics.avoid: Do not promise universal relevance without explaining the specific connection.

mechanics.mechanic: State the major concepts, categories, practical tools, and sequence the audience will encounter before beginning the main explanation.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use for dense educational material with several layers of theory and application.
mechanics.avoid: Do not provide an exhaustive outline that removes curiosity or creates expectations the material cannot fulfill.

mechanics.mechanic: Give a functional definition, then distinguish the concept from nearby ideas by describing what counts as success, failure, or limitation.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when an everyday term has multiple technical meanings or is commonly misunderstood.
mechanics.avoid: Do not rely on a dictionary-style definition without showing how the concept behaves in practice.

mechanics.mechanic: Start with the core causal relationship, introduce the relevant components, and use a familiar analogy before adding technical detail.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when translating specialized science or systems thinking for a general audience.
mechanics.avoid: Do not let the analogy replace the mechanism, and do not introduce more technical vocabulary than the explanation requires.

mechanics.function: Reframe the guiding question around constraints
mechanics.mechanic: Shift from asking what enables an outcome to asking what limits or interrupts it; use that constraint as the organizing principle for the rest of the discussion.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when the audience needs to understand why an intervention or training method should work.
mechanics.avoid: Do not treat one limiting factor as universally decisive across all people, contexts, or tasks.

mechanics.function: Use a category framework to organize complexity
mechanics.mechanic: Partition a complicated system into a small set of functional components, then revisit each component with its role, failure mode, and practical implication.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when many interacting variables would otherwise create a confusing explanation.
mechanics.avoid: Do not imply that the categories operate independently when the point depends on their interaction.

mechanics.function: Pair each recommendation with its rationale and boundary conditions
mechanics.mechanic: Present a practical protocol, explain the mechanism it targets, identify what it is not designed to improve, and note relevant safety or skill constraints.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use whenever an explanation moves from evidence to action.
mechanics.avoid: Do not present numerical ranges or procedures as universal prescriptions without accounting for experience, goals, technique, and individual differences.

mechanics.function: Offer optional depth without interrupting the main path
mechanics.mechanic: Give the general audience a concise explanation while directing technically inclined readers to a separate, more detailed source or section.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when one audience needs accessibility and another wants methodological or mechanistic depth.
mechanics.avoid: Do not make the supplementary material essential to understanding the main argument.

mechanics.function: Close sections with synthesis and forward linkage
mechanics.mechanic: Summarize what the audience should now understand, connect it to the larger framework, and use that conclusion to introduce the next section.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use after a dense conceptual or procedural block to preserve orientation and momentum.
mechanics.avoid: Do not merely repeat preceding points; add the implication that makes the transition meaningful.
